1. (Currently amended) A catheter system for delivering ultrasonic energy to a treatment site within a body lumen, the catheter comprising: a tubular body having a proximal end, a distal end and an energy delivery section positioned between the proximal end and the distal end; a plurality of ultrasound radiating members positioned within the energy delivery section, the plurality of ultrasound radiating members being allocated into at least three electrical groups comprising more than one ultrasound radiating member each; wherein the ultrasound radiating members of one electrical group are spatially interdigitated with the ultrasound radiating members of at least two other electrical groups in a non-uniform spatial distribution pattern.

2. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the plurality of ultrasound radiating members are mounted on an inner core, wherein the inner core is configured for insertion into the tubular body, and wherein the inner core comprises a non-conductive material.

3. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, further comprising at least one therapeutic compound delivery lumen that extends through the tubular body and terminates at least one outlet positioned in the energy delivery section, wherein the therapeutic compound delivery lumen is positioned radially offset from the ultrasound radiating members.

4. (Cancelled)

5. (Cancelled)

6. (Currently amended) A system for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the system comprising: a first ultrasound catheter and a second ultrasound catheter, each of the first and the second ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section having at least one ultrasound element mounted on an elongate inner core, the tubular body also including at least one fluid delivery lumen; and a control system connected to and configured to operate both the first and the second elongate inner cores with independent phase control.

7. (Currently amended) The system of Claim 6, wherein the control system operates both the first and the second elongate inner cores simultaneously with a predetermined phase offset between the first and the second ultrasound catheters.

8. (Currently amended) The system of Claim 7, wherein the control system is configured to independently control the ultrasound radiating members on the first and the second elongate inner cores with respect to frequency modulation.

9. (Currently amended) A method for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the method comprising: advancing an ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element and at least one fluid delivery lumen; advancing the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter to a treatment site in the patient's pulmonary artery; inflating a balloon on the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter; delivering a thrombolytic drug to the treatment site through the at least one fluid delivery lumen at a controlled flow rate; and emitting ultrasonic energy at a frequency between 20 kHz and 100 kHz to thereby promote diffusion of the thrombolytic drug at the treatment site.

10. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 9, wherein delivering the thrombolytic drug and emitting ultrasonic energy are performed simultaneously with the ultrasonic energy enhancing thrombolytic efficacy.

11. (Currently amended) An ultrasound catheter for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element mounted on an elongate inner core and at least one fluid delivery lumen, the tubular body defining a guidewire lumen extending through the proximal portion and the ultrasound energy delivery section, wherein the guidewire lumen is positioned eccentrically relative to the ultrasound element.

12. (Currently amended) The ultrasound catheter of Claim 11, wherein the guidewire lumen extends through the at least one ultrasound element with a minimum radial separation of at least 0.5 mm.

13. (Currently amended) The ultrasound catheter of Claim 11, further comprising at least one balloon positioned at the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter, wherein the balloon is constructed from a compliant elastomeric material.
